setupText.title: Setup Panel Help
lines: Select board size and tray type, then click on 'Make Board'.
Either create a puzzle or start a game.
Puzzle: click on pieces and tiles; place, shift, or return, 'Freeze Puzzle' to accept.
Game: click on 'Starting Position'.
Use undo/redo and rewind/FF (Game Panel) to change your mind (note scroll window, currently buggy).
(Factory trays not yet supported, same as Real trays.)

moveText.title: Move Panel Help
lines: To specify a move, select a piece and a tile.
To specify a capture, select two pieces, first captures second.
Captures require a target piece, moves require a tile.
Buttons are enabled if the combination of selected piece(s) and tile(s) form an eligible move.
To be legal, a move must be both eligible and allowed. It is disallowed if out of plane, out of range, blocked, etc.
This separation converts the move buttons into affordances, good user ergonomics. They are only enabled when eligible.
Some moves require multiple piece and tile selections (castling, en passant, fission, etc.) - click order is important.
To select a stack, select both the bishop and duke subpieces.
In a fission, first subpiece goes with the first target piece, or if no target, with the first tile.
To deselect, click again. To clear all selections, click off board.
This idiom is consistent and becomes intuitive pretty quickly.

gambitText.title: Gambit Panel Help
lines: Use gambits to freeze the current advsq.
Assemble a set to understand a tactical situation.
Then decide on a move.
You can freeze quadrants (typical).
Linear moves (stride must be on an end tile).
Duplex moves (stride must be on a duplex tile, duke face quads only).
Overlap moves (queen and stack only).
Stride must be one of the four overlap tiles (brook, qtile, hotspot, Feynman).
INCOMPLETE, use with caution.

advsqText.title: Advsq Panel Help
lines: Reveals the nonintuitive nature of 3D moves.
Place a source tile.
Grow and shrink the advancement square into the quadrant (1-60).
Or use the perimeter box for direct entry (0-7).
To keep the NxN structure of advsqs clear, they are allowed to extend off the board.
You cannot move to these tiles, they have no effect on the game, just on your visualization.
Use the stride box to 'walk' the perimeter.
Note the diagnostic fields that reveal the advsq's properties.
You can move the src tile rectilinear with the keyboard (ijk, IJK).
Rotate through the quads 'Next Quad'.
Rotate through the planes 'Next Plane'.
Rotate through the pieces 'Next Piece'.
Change the visibility of offboard tiles.

gameText.title: Game Panel Help
lines: 3DC uses a logarithmic undo system: 4 sequential buffers.
Setup - Moves - Gambits - Advsqs.
Undo/redo traverses within and across them.
Rewind traverses from first to last, then across them.
Save captures them to the clipboard.
Load restarts the game from the clipboard.
Makes it easy to share games, puzzles, and lessons.

cameraText.title: Camera Panel Help
lines: Zoom in and out.
Ascend and descend (view angle), tradeoff tile perspective with obscured tiles.
4 points of views provided, basically all four vertical edges.
(The top view is basically useless for play, but useful for diagnostics.)

compassText.title: Compass Panel Help
lines: Eventually will allow slip and slide of advsqs along planes and quads.
yada

viewerText.title: Viewer Panel Help
lines: Show and hide the trays.
Change tray gap and level separation, use as needed.
Put the board into a slow rotation around the z-axis, with variable range and speed.
Combine with the camera panel to maximize the clarity of the current position.

diagnosticsText.title: Diagnostics Panel Help
lines: Useful for debugging code.
Limited use for play.
